correctness.rationale: For the real symmetric Laplacian, PBH excludes controllability exactly when a nonzero eigenspace vector vanishes at the actuator vertices. An unactuated pair of leaves on one side admits an eigenvalue-one difference there, forcing at least p−1 and q−1 selected leaves. For λ≠1 the zero selected leaves pin the hubs, and the other leaf equations and positive spine-edge recurrence pin the entire eigenvector. At λ=1 the hubs are pinned independently of any hub inputs. The interior satisfies the Dirichlet path recurrence, whose distinct modes have eigenvalues 2t(1−cos(jπ/L)); for L=1 the interior is empty. Off resonance the two zero leaf-sum equations eliminate the last leaves. At resonance the residual invisible space for the baseline leaf set is one-dimensional and its remaining leaf values are −t times the adjacent endpoint entries, both nonzero. A last leaf or a nonnodal interior vertex suppresses it; a hub or a position with L dividing ji cannot. There are L−gcd(L,j) eligible interior vertices. For rational t, 2−1/t is a rational algebraic integer in (−2,2), hence −1,0,1, giving exactly the stated divisibilities and conductances. For ordinary zero forcing the baseline leaf set works on adjacent hubs but stalls on a nonempty interior; fully blackening one bundle allows the spine and the last leaf to be forced with one extra seed.
residual_risks: The rank replay covers bounded rational instances only. The proof covers positive real conductances under the fixed common-spine and unit-pendant assumptions; it gives no conditioning guarantee.

evidence: The unweighted multiplicity result gives eigenvalue-one multiplicity equal to the number of leaves minus one when all pendant pair distances are 2 modulo 3; the cross-bundle distance here is L+2.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct content is the exact all-positive-conductance resonance set for the two-hub family, with all optimal coordinate placements, their sine-node exclusion, and the rational sub-classification. The unweighted multiplicity jump is prior coverage, and its resonant cardinality also follows by combining the old multiplicity obstruction with the simple zero-forcing upper bound. Generic robustness-vs-fixed-Laplacian distinctions and analogous budgets on other graph families are not new here.
residual_risks: Full texts of the cited Dai and Parlangeli papers were not available in the attempted lawful routes; a stronger fixed-matrix selection theorem remains a possible unassessed overlap. No same-day discovery priority or exhaustive novelty is inferred.

value.rationale: This fixed-Laplacian budget is a natural control design quantity. The classification predicts exactly when changing one common conductance causes the fixed-weight control savings over support-based forcing to vanish, and which interior locations can or cannot rescue the budget at those weights. Knowing the number of inputs alone cannot answer the placement question, and knowing just the unweighted multiplicity cannot guide a continuously tunable network.
residual_risks: No result about near-resonance numerical margins, energy or unequal edge conductances is claimed.
